To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a spatial two-stage model can be used to postprocess numerical forecasts of precipitation fields and produce sharp, calibrated probabilistic forecasts of spatial precipitation fields; (2) the spatial two-stage model provides a more accurate description of the spatial distribution of precipitation than a spatial two-component model; (3) the spatial two-component model is a special case of the spatial two-stage; and (4) the spatial two-stages model outperforms the spatial two-component and reference models.

the spatial version of a mixture of a Gamma distribution and a point mass at 0, with a Gaussian process for the Gamma parameter, is an effective and flexible model for spatial precipitation accumulation.
a two-stage spatial statistical model for precipitation accumulation is well suited for postprocessing numerical forecasts of precipitation accumulation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a spatial two-stage model for probabilistic quantitative precipitation field forecasts, which is based on the information provided by numerical weather forecasts.
the development of a new statistical methodology to improve short-range precipitation forecasts.
the development of a statistical model that can produce probabilistic precipitation forecasts at multiple locations simultaneously, and is applicable to any numerical forecast.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed two-stage spatial model is a promising approach for post-processing precipitation forecasts from numerical weather prediction systems.

the two-stage spatial models can produce calibrated, sharp, spatially coherent, probabilistic predictions for daily precipitation accumulation at multiple locations simultaneously, and outperform reference forecasts.
the two-stage spatial postprocessing technique provides an effective and flexible tool to produce probabilistic forecasts of spatial precipitation fields.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the spatial two-stage model is an excellent tool for producing spatially correlated probabilistic precipitation forecasts.

the proposed model can be used to produce sharp and well-calibrated probabilistic forecasts of daily precipitation at multiple sites, given forecasts of precipitation from a numerical weather prediction model.
the proposed model is a promising tool for probabilistic short-range quantitative precipitation field forecasting.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the two-stage spatial approach can be used to generate sharp and accurate probabilistic forecasts of areally averaged precipitation accumulation.
spatial correlation can be modeled in the context of a two-stage spatial probabilistic model for precipitation, without having to model the marginal distribution of precipitation.

spatially distributed forecasts of precipitation can be obtained from numerical weather forecasts using a simple statistical model that is flexible enough to capture spatial correlation and the right marginal distribution of precipitation.
